svg.title: Sisukas authentication system architecture
svg.desc: The student signs in through the sign-in UI, which uses the frontend modules/auth public API. Its internal Better Auth client calls authHttpHandler at /api/auth/* inside the backend's authentication boundary; the handler applies the account-linking policy, sends magic links through Resend and stores user, account, session and verification rows in PostgreSQL. Google and GitHub OAuth are planned. The auth module passes the canonical user.id to the app/auth data lifecycle, which loads or resets user-owned data. Application requests carry the session cookie; extractSession calls resolveAuthenticatedSession() to obtain the canonical user.id, and routes check ownership before reading or writing plans, favourites, grades and calendar preferences. PostgreSQL adds constraints and RLS policies for the roles they target.
svg.text: Routes enforce ownership on the canonical user.id. RLS policies apply only to the roles they target;
the Supabase-oriented RLS tests do not show enforcement for Better Auth or Drizzle runtime queries.
